English: Counting Room
A modest stone chamber where ledgers are kept and deals are tallied, lending legitimacy to the markets transactions.
Merchant Booth
A humble canvas booth for trading wares, marking the Jewish quarters first step into local commerce.
Trade Arcade
A row of wooden stalls and awnings, offering a more stable venue for the quarters burgeoning merchants.
Bookstall Lane
A bustling lane lined with book stalls and scribes, a hub of learning and commerce renowned beyond the city walls.
Moneylenders' Office
A reinforced office for moneylending and credit, guarded and equipped to handle valuables and sensitive negotiations.
Jewelers Shop
A secure, stone-built shop where skilled craftsmen cut gems and mint precious wares, attracting traders from afar.
Cloth Hall
A grand market hall for textiles and luxury fabrics, with vaulted ceilings and guarded entries, bustling with wealthy patrons.
Market Gallery
A covered market of stone and timber, with multiple galleries for artisans, traders, and guilds, offering both protection and prestige.
Commerce House
A stately headquarters for trade guilds and merchant councils, supervising contracts and mediating disputes with authority.
Grand Merchant Quarter
The entire district transformed into an opulent center of commerce, protected by walls and patrolled by guards, drawing merchants from across continents.
